feedback.problem:
Evaluate the following integral of a vector-valued function. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{4}^{16}⟨6t-1,\,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}⟩\,\text{d}t=⟨$
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}} $⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{4}^{16}⟨6t-1,\,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}⟩\,\text{d}t & =⟨{\int }_{4}^{16}(6t-1)\,\text{d}t,\,{\int }_{4}^{16}\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,\text{d}t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

For the first component,

$$
\int (6t-1)\,\text{d}t=3{t}^{2}-t.
$$

For the second component,

$$
\int \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,\text{d}t=\sqrt{t}.
$$

Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{4}^{16}⟨6t-1,\,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}⟩\,\text{d}t & =⟨(3{t}^{2}-t){|}_{4}^{16},\,(\sqrt{t}){|}_{4}^{16}⟩ \\  & =⟨(3\cdot {16}^{2}-16)-(3\cdot {4}^{2}-4),\,4-2⟩ \\  & =⟨(768-16)-(48-4),\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨752-44,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨708,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨708,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
